en.name: Boniface IX
en.summary: A Roman pope of the Western Schism whose long reign stabilized the Roman line financially and territorially despite the ongoing rival Avignon papacy.
en.body: Boniface IX, continuing the Roman line of popes during the Western Schism, proved a capable administrator who expanded indulgence sales and other revenue sources to fund the reconquest of Papal States territory that had slipped away amid the schism's chaos. His reign brought relative stability to the Roman obedience even as the rival Avignon line under Clement VII and then Benedict XIII continued to claim legitimacy.
